headline: High: shared filesystem and write-capable document processing create default-path data leakage and cascading-error risks; prompt injection is lower due to no direct shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has files for data sources, validation results, and documentation, while B can read/write files and parse documents. A direct injection path is plausible only if A’s outputs are manually or file-fed into B; no shared channel is documented, so this is lower severity and uncertain.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into files that agent_b parses as instructions
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace without content filtering
mitigations: Separate input and output directories for the two agents
Strip instruction-like text from files before B ingests them
Use read-only mounts for A’s outputs
Add a manual review step before B processes A-generated files

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches validation results and documentation; B can read files and has allowlisted network egress. If they share a workspace, B can ingest A’s artifacts and potentially transmit derived content to external services. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default file-based workflows, though not proven.
conditions: IF agent_a writes validation results into a directory readable by agent_b
IF agent_b sends parsed document contents or extracted text to its allowlisted network endpoints
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate volumes
Disable B network egress for sensitive runs
Redact validation outputs before B reads them
Use per-run temp directories with automatic cleanup
Log and review all outbound requests from B

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can install packages and write outputs; B can install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. Their overlapping write and execution capabilities create a realistic conflict if they share mutable paths, even though B has docker isolation and no locking is documented.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same writable directory
IF package installation or subprocess execution targets shared state
mitigations: Assign disjoint working directories
Serialize access to shared artifacts
Pin dependencies per agent
Run B in a separate container per job
Use file locks on any shared mutable path

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces validation results and documentation, and B processes documents. If B treats A’s outputs as authoritative, errors in A can cascade into B’s downstream parsing or actions. B’s sandboxing helps, but no verification step between them is documented, so the default-path risk remains.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated validation results as source-of-truth
IF no human or automated verification step checks A’s outputs before B acts
mitigations: Insert a verification gate between A and B
Require schema validation on A’s outputs
Have B cite provenance for every field it uses
Reject A outputs that fail checksum or signature checks
Review a sample of B’s downstream actions daily

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. A is open-source with no secrets handled; B exposes privacy-policy and docs URLs but no conflicting compliance constraint is stated. With only docs-only evidence, a compliance breach is not established.
conditions: IF a future deployment routes regulated data to a noncompliant endpoint
IF retention or residency policies differ from the documented defaults
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling before deployment
Review vendor privacy and retention terms
Avoid sending regulated data until policies are verified
